notes:
What's new in Vekrun 0.7.3

• A key in your .env now counts: if the .env you let Factory use already sets RAILS_MASTER_KEY, the Rails encryption key is shown as covered straight away, and Factory no longer waits for config/master.key. The same goes for any other value the tests need that your .env (or a variable you gave) already sets. Vekrun checks only the variable's name; the agent never sees its value.
• Before Start, it's clear what stops the work: anything required is marked in amber as "Needed before Factory can start", optional items are labelled Optional, and items you've already given show a check. Pressing Start while something is still needed takes you to it and briefly highlights it (a still outline if you've turned on Reduce motion).
• "One thing first" now says exactly what's left, for example "1 thing needed before start", and it disappears once nothing is in the way. "Start without it" says which tests will fail.
• The request box grows as you type or paste, up to a comfortable height, and scrolls after that.
• The stack line under the request reads properly: "Stack: Ruby on Rails, found in the repository · Reconsider".
• Engineering Memory Graph: "+N more linked" and "+N more symbols" now open the full list. Click one, or Tab to it and press Enter, and the inspector shows every linked decision, spec, outcome, incident and deployment, grouped by type with a count for each. Long lists in the inspector (knowledge, symbols, dependencies, callers, linked tests, the file pairs under a relationship, and a decision's linked code) show their first items, then "Show all", and get a filter box. Nothing the graph counts is hidden any more.
• A Work Item's Workspace is now one screen for the whole run: the same header, one step bar (Workspace → Dependencies → Plan → Building → Testing → Proof → Your review) and Live output, from setting up to your review. The Council no longer swaps in a different page mid-run: it is the Plan step, its stage shows inside that step ("Debate, 3 of 4"), its progress appears in Live output, and its proposals and debate open on the same page from the Plan step. Steps only move forward; when your tests run alongside the plan, both show as working. Live output is always open, and opening the Council from the Map now selects the Workspace tab it shows.
• Setting up a Rails project now names what went wrong, in plain words, and fixes what it safely can by itself. A Gemfile.lock made on a Mac (listing only macOS) no longer stops the Factory: Vekrun adds Linux to a copy inside the build machine so the gems install, says so in the run's log, and leaves your Gemfile.lock untouched. If you like, one click on the Work Item ("Add Linux to Gemfile.lock in this pull request") adds it to the work as its own commit, with the exact lines shown first.
• Other setup problems are handled the same way: a gem that needs a system library (pg, mysql2, rmagick and more) gets it installed in the build machine; the Ruby your project names is installed; a lockfile made with an old Bundler uses one that runs. Only if your gems really would change (a different version, a new gem) does Vekrun stop, and it says exactly which.
• Gems from a private source: the Work Item asks for that source's login right there, keeps it as the project's secret, gives it only to Bundler while it installs (never to agents or tests, never shown in logs), and carries on by itself once you save it.
• A setup that stops now reads "Needs you", not "Failed · Critical": nothing in your project changed and no agent ran. The card shows the Work Item's short title instead of your whole request, says the cause first and the one next step, with the command, exit code and last log lines (secrets removed) under Technical details.
• A Rails app that also has a JavaScript test script is now checked with its Rails tests, not `yarn test`.
• Dashboards in a project's Docker Compose file that no test uses (Kibana, pgAdmin, Grafana and the like) are no longer started in the build machine, leaving its memory to the tests; the run's notes say which were skipped.
• Signing in a coding agent or GitHub is now offered inside Vekrun wherever a message used to say to run a command in Terminal.
• Your tests, visibly running: while Vekrun runs a project's tests once before the change (the baseline), the Live output now shows them as they go — failures and the runner's summary as they appear, and one progress line that updates in place: "Baseline tests: 1,240 run · 3 failing so far · 6m 12s". When a previous run of the same suite exists it adds "usually ~14 min" (an estimate from that run). minitest/`rails test`, RSpec, pytest, jest, vitest, `go test` and `cargo test` are understood; anything else shows its lines. Test output goes through the same redaction as everything else, so a secret it prints never reaches the screen.
• No more silent waits: if the tests print nothing for a while, the progress line says so and whether they are still working ("still running, last output 45s ago, CPU busy"). A run that is truly stuck — no output and no CPU for 5 minutes — is called out, and stopped at 10 minutes so the Work Item carries on.
• The Work Item says what it is doing: "Running baseline tests · 6m" instead of a bare "Preparing", and "Waiting for baseline tests · 8m" if the change is ready before they are.
• The build no longer waits for the baseline when it doesn't have to: when the project's tests use no database server or other service in the VM, they run in a private copy of the checkout and the agent starts building at once; their result is only needed when the change is tested. When they do share a database or a service with the agent's own test runs, the build still waits, and Vekrun says exactly why (Settings → Factory: factory.speed.baseline_beside_build).
• Tests that run the VM out of memory are caught: Rails' parallel test workers beside services like Elasticsearch and Kibana could exhaust a 4 GB VM, a worker was killed, and the run then waited silently until its 15- or 30-minute limit. Vekrun now watches every test run (the baseline, the agent's and Vekrun's own) and stops one that is out of memory and no longer moving, saying so in plain words. For the baseline it then runs the tests again with fewer parallel workers, sized to the memory the VM has free, and keeps that number for every later test run of the project, its proof included.
• Pressing Start again on the Factory page no longer starts a running request a second time. The composer now shows what's running in the project ("Running: … · Dependencies · 9m · Open"), and Start on a request that's already running opens it. A Work Item that's running can't be started again on top of itself (Run again, Continue, a double click or a retry): it keeps running untouched, and you stop it first if you want to start over. A different request can still start while another one runs.
• Everything now belongs to a project: the Board, Work, the Inbox (and its badge and notifications), Brainstorm, handoffs, PR Guardian, Project Delivery, ticket plans, CI runs, deployments and the command line and MCP lists show only the project you have open — nothing from another project appears while you work in this one. Tickets from your trackers join a project through its repository links; tickets that don't map to any project wait under "Not linked to a project" on the Board, with one click to link them. Older Work Items are given their project automatically, and any Vekrun can't place are listed for you to assign.
• Old backups from earlier versions are now cleaned up automatically. Versions before 0.7.2 saved a full copy of your data before every update and never removed one, so a long-time install could hold tens of gigabytes of them. Vekrun now keeps the newest complete one and removes the rest, along with any unfinished copies a failed backup left behind. Your current data and the read-only copy kept from the 0.7.2 move are never touched.
• An update that lacks disk space now says so before it starts: how much it needs and how much is free, with nothing written and nothing installed. It offers to make room by clearing old backups, shows you exactly which files would go and how much space that frees, and continues once you confirm.
• The same offer appears if the one-time move to the new database (from 0.7.1 or earlier) stops for lack of disk space.
• A backup that fails or is interrupted no longer leaves a partial file behind.
• Correction to the 0.7.2 notes: "the newest five backups are kept" applied only to backups made by 0.7.2 and later. Older backups are now cleaned up as described above.
• The Board is easier to read and act on: a ticket opens in a full detail view with its description laid out as clean fields (Epic, Spike, Depends on, Design, links you can click), its checklist, status, move-to actions, related decisions from Engineering Memory, and a prominent Start Work. The List view is a tidy ID / Title / Status table with a copyable ticket id, Kanban cards show id chips and select boxes, and "Sync now" is right there when a tracker is connected.
